answer: Interleaved-arrival windows. Each identity must keep its request inter-arrivals within a narrow band around a per-window median, and new identities must first produce a crystal-clear steady cadence across several consecutive windows before full traffic rights. Enforcement is per-window: bursty signups fail the ridge test because their arrival gaps deviate too far from the median shape, while a lone attacker must spread registrations across time to pass. A gale of parallel identities arriving together gets throttled to the slowest admissible cadence.
